challenge.method: Tested an upstream distribution without NOTICE, a derivative with relevant attributions in accompanying documentation, and an attribution concerning only omitted material. Compared §4(d) with the adjacent §4(c) Source-notice requirement and ASF 1.1's documentation acknowledgment.
challenge.results: Without upstream NOTICE, §4(d) creates no duty to supply one. When the condition holds, readable attributions in accompanying documentation satisfy the location requirement. Other permitted locations are a distributed NOTICE, accompanying Source, or the derivative's generated display where such notices normally appear. An attribution pertaining to no part of the derivative may be omitted. Section 4(c) separately preserves applicable copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from upstream Source in distributed derivative Source. The older edition's acknowledgment clause has different wording and scope. [ASF version 1.1](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-1.1)

limitations: Whether a particular distribution qualifies as a Derivative Work and which attributions pertain to it depend on the facts. Other §4 obligations and ASF release-packaging policies have separate scope.
